catalog.name: Atmosphere
catalog.description: Atmospheric composition and aerosol datasets from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), including aerosol optical depth, atmospheric composition, and radiation measurements.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Data provided by NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS). Contact: earthdata-support@nasa.gov

info.name: License
info.content: NASA data is generally available for public use. Please check individual dataset licenses and cite appropriately.

info.name: Coverage
info.content: Global coverage with various temporal and spatial resolutions depending on the specific mission and instrument.

members.name: Aerosols
members.description: Aerosol optical depth and related measurements providing insights into atmospheric particles, air quality, and climate interactions.

members.name: MODIS Aqua Aerosol Optical Depth
members.description: Daily aerosol optical depth measurements from MODIS on the Aqua satellite, combining land and ocean retrievals.

info.name: Background
info.content: Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) measures the extinction of solar radiation by aerosol particles in the atmosphere. It's a key parameter for air quality monitoring and climate studies.

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: 2002 to present, updated daily

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 1 km at nadir, aggregated to various resolutions

info.name: Applications
info.content: Air quality monitoring, dust storm tracking, smoke detection, climate research

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

members.name: SWDB Aerosol Angstrom Exponent
members.description: Aerosol Angstrom Exponent from SeaWiFS Deep Blue algorithm, indicating aerosol particle size characteristics.

info.name: Background
info.content: The Angstrom Exponent relates to aerosol particle size - higher values indicate smaller particles (urban pollution, smoke) while lower values indicate larger particles (dust).

info.name: Parameter Range
info.content: Typically ranges from 0 (large particles like dust) to 2+ (small particles like smoke/pollution)

info.name: Applications
info.content: Aerosol type discrimination, air quality studies, source identification

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA SeaWiFS mission team, Deep Blue algorithm development team

members.name: Radiation
members.description: Atmospheric radiation measurements including outgoing longwave radiation critical for Earth's energy balance studies.

members.name: PREFIRE Outgoing Longwave Radiative Flux
members.description: Outgoing longwave radiative flux measurements from the PREFIRE (Polar Radiant Energy in the Far-InfraRed Experiment) mission.

info.name: Background
info.content: PREFIRE measures far-infrared radiation emitted by Earth, particularly important in polar regions for understanding energy balance and climate change impacts.

info.name: Mission Focus
info.content: Polar regions - Arctic and Antarctic energy balance

info.name: Wavelength Range
info.content: Far-infrared spectrum (5-50 μm) previously unmeasured from space

info.name: Applications
info.content: Climate modeling, polar climate studies, ice-atmosphere interactions, global energy budget

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA PREFIRE mission team, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory

members.name: Upper Atmosphere
members.description: Upper atmospheric measurements from specialized instruments providing insights into stratospheric and mesospheric conditions.

members.name: MLS Temperature 46hPa
members.description: Microwave Limb Sounder (MLS) temperature measurements at 46hPa pressure level in the stratosphere.

info.name: Background
info.content: MLS provides precise measurements of atmospheric temperature in the upper troposphere and stratosphere using microwave observations of thermal emission.

info.name: Pressure Level
info.content: 46hPa (~20-22 km altitude, lower stratosphere)

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: 2004 to present from Aura satellite

info.name: Applications
info.content: Stratospheric research, ozone layer studies, atmospheric dynamics, climate monitoring

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MLS team, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
